title: A 27B model on one 32 GB Intel card
subtitle: A measured, attributed and published 4-bit quantization of a 27-billion-parameter hybrid recurrent-attention open-weight model for an Intel Arc Pro GPU

stats.label: sustained output throughput over the mixed 4-bit and 8-bit control, 64 clients
higher perplexity than full precision on an 8-document diagnostic set
tokens per second total at 32 clients, 1,536-token prompts, prefix caching on

lede: The base model, a 27-billion-parameter hybrid recurrent-attention open-weight model, does not fit in BF16 on a 32 GB Intel Arc Pro GPU, and I needed it to, with room left for context and concurrency. I built a 4-bit-weight quantization that fits it, ran a four-arm experiment to attribute exactly where the speed came from, and published the model with its card on Hugging Face. The model card states the trade-off in plain numbers. Fitting a large model on a smaller card is routine on NVIDIA hardware with mature tooling. On a new Intel architecture, with a stock XPU build of vLLM and no forked kernels, it was not.
quote: I took the throughput and stated the cost.
evidence: LLM quantization (4-bit): a weight-only W4A16 recipe for a 27-billion-parameter hybrid model, rounded from hash-checked weights with no calibration data, at 3.33% higher perplexity than full precision.
Intel GPU inference: a 27B model fitted on one 32 GB Intel Arc Pro GPU under the unmodified Intel XPU build of vLLM, 1,798 tokens per second in total at 32 clients.
Experimental design for performance attribution: a four-arm experiment crossed over across two cards, attributing a +36% sustained throughput gain at 64 clients to what changed between arms.
Model publication and provenance: a model published on Hugging Face with per-module manifests, hash-replayed measurements and release validation of 433 files per checkpoint.
author: Corey James
